linuxVmDirectoryHint: The parent directory must already exist. Only the final directory named after the VM is created. An existing directory can be reused; existing files are never overwritten.
linuxVmNamePathHint: The name is also used as a directory name. Path separators and the names '.' and '..' are not allowed.
transferDownloadUnavailableTitle: Cannot verify the original download record
transferDownloadUnavailableHint: The record may have expired or been removed, or the service may be temporarily unavailable. The local record is retained. Check before querying again or explicitly forgetting it; downloads are not restarted automatically.
packagePreviewRecoveryHint: The preview request from before reload has been recovered. Only its original result is queried. Review and confirm again before importing.
packageImportRecoveryHintRestored: The submitted import request has been recovered. Only its original result is queried; the import is not repeated. Unsubmitted edits and confirmations are not restored.
packageExportRecoveryHint: The submitted export request has been recovered. Only its original result is queried; export and download preparation are not repeated automatically. Read a new plan and confirm before another export.
transferDownloadRecoveryHint: The download record for this tab has been recovered. Query its original status first. Files are not downloaded automatically, and browser download progress is not restored.
transferDownloadDeleteUnknown: Deletion of the original download record is unconfirmed. Query its status or explicitly retry deletion. Download links remain unavailable.
transferDownloadForgetHint: Forget only this tab’s download record. This does not remove the server download session or exported files, or automatically prepare another download.
diskDefaultsMenuHint: App optimization compression and the CPU cores used by new disk operations.
diskDefaultsScope: Shared with the host App. New disk operation forms use the saved CPU selection once when opened; existing edits and requests keep their own choices.
diskDefaultsCompressionHint: Shared by App and WebUI disk optimization. Ordinary disk conversion and Linux image preparation keep their own compression options.
diskDefaultsCpuHint: Defaults for disk tool processes, separate from VM and GPU CPU affinity. An empty selection leaves the process unbound; you can override it for an individual operation.
diskDefaultsSaved: Defaults saved. They will be used when preparing new operations.
usbAcmApplyFailureReason: Application did not complete. Check the current state before explicitly applying again.
usbAcmUnavailableReason: The USB device state cannot currently be read.
usbAcmMismatchReason: The current USB port configuration differs from the saved target.
usbAcmIdentityReason: The USB port configuration could not be verified. Check the device state before making changes.
usbAcmControllerReason: The USB controller is not currently bound.
usbAcmPortReason: A configured serial port is not currently available.
usbAcmMenuHint: Manage the host USB serial gadget and check VM port ownership.
usbAcmScope: Configure the host’s USB ACM gadget shared with the App. This is separate from USB passthrough rules; each VM still needs its own serial-port assignment.
usbAcmDefaults: No shared settings have been saved. These are defaults; opening this page does not apply them.
usbAcmApplied: The saved target is currently applied.
usbAcmNotApplied: The saved target is not confirmed as applied.
usbAcmNoOwners: No VM currently owns an ACM port.
usbAcmOccupied: An active VM owns a port. Stop the affected VM before changing or rebinding the USB gadget.
usbAcmEnableHint: Expose serial ports through this device’s USB connection.
usbAcmPortsHint: Choose 1–6 ports. Saving the host target does not assign these ports to VMs.
usbAcmApplySavedHint: Apply the latest saved target without changing its values.
usbAcmDisconnectHint: Applying changes may re-enumerate the USB device and temporarily disconnect USB connections, including a WebUI connection over USB.
usbAcmConfirmDisconnect: I understand that USB connections may be interrupted.
usbAcmConflictHint: Your edits were preserved. Review them against the latest saved target, then confirm the operation again.
usbAcmRebase: Keep edits and review latest target
usbAcmStale: The displayed state is outdated. Refresh before applying changes.
usbAcmUnknown: The operation receipt is unknown. Query the original request; do not repeat the save or apply.
usbAcmUncertain: Persistence or application is uncertain. New operations are blocked while the original result is checked.
usbAcmOperationApplied: The operation reported that the target was applied.
usbAcmSavedNotApplied: The target was saved, but application failed. Check the current state and use “Apply saved settings” when available.
hostPreferencesMenuHint: Automatic hugepage reservation, SD card optimization and log clearing before startup.
hostPreferencesScope: Shared with the host App. Changes apply to subsequent VM starts; they do not change VMs that are already running.
hostPreferencesHugepagesHint: Before starting a VM that uses the hugepage pool, attempt to reserve the required capacity. This does not change the VM’s memory mode or guarantee that enough memory is available.
hostPreferencesSdcardHint: Before VM startup, attempt the host App’s SD card access optimization for external storage. Availability and benefit depend on the device, permissions and storage path.
hostPreferencesLogsHint: Remove the VM’s previous logs before its next start. Leave this off to keep logs for troubleshooting.
hostPreferencesStale: The displayed preferences are outdated. Refresh before saving.
hostPreferencesDefaults: Shared settings have not been initialized. The displayed values are defaults; reading this page does not save them.
hostPreferencesUncertain: The saved state is uncertain. Further changes are blocked while the original operation is checked.
hostPreferencesConflictHint: Your edits have been preserved. Review them against the latest values, then confirm the save again.
hostPreferencesRebase: Keep edits and use latest version
hostPreferencesUnknown: The save receipt is unknown. Query the original request; do not submit it again.
hostPreferencesSaved: Preferences saved. They apply to subsequent VM starts.
packageImportHostHint: Import an existing package on the host, or upload a package from this browser. Preview the package before choosing the target directory and network mappings.
packageImportUnavailable: Package import is unavailable with the current service or permissions.
packageImportSourceHint: Enter a .vmpkg main file or a .NNN volume path. The service locates the main file and reads a preview. Changing the path requires a new preview.
packageImportPending: A preview or import request is awaiting confirmation. Only the original request is queried; it will not be resubmitted.
packageImportVolumes: Split volume count (0 means one file)
packageImportTargetHint: Enter an absolute directory path on the device running DroidVM. Import writes files and registers a VM. Check available space and existing contents first.
packageImportConflictIpv4: An IPv4 range conflict prevents creating this packaged network.
packageImportConflictIpv6: An IPv6 range conflict prevents creating this packaged network.
packageImportConflictUplink: An uplink conflict prevents creating this packaged network.
packageImportCreateUnavailable: The current configuration does not allow creating this packaged network.
packageImportNoNetworks: This package has no networks requiring a choice.
packageImportStaleNetworks: The previous network choices do not match the latest preview. Review and select them again.
packageImportResetNetworks: Select networks from the latest preview
packageImportInvalid: Enter a valid host target directory and an available action for every network in the preview.
packageImportConfirmHint: Import reads the package from this preview, writes to the target directory, applies the network choices and registers the VM. Changes to the package or configuration reject the operation. Failure or cancellation may leave files or committed configuration; rollback is not guaranteed.
packageImportConfirm: I reviewed the package, target directory and network choices and confirm starting the import.
packageImportUnknown: The result is unknown. Only the original request is queried, without automatic resubmission. A missing record does not prove that it was never executed.
packageImportRegistrationUnknown: VM registration is uncertain. A candidate record is available for inspection only; it does not prove successful import.
packageImportNotRegistered: VM registration has not been confirmed.
packageImportCleanupComplete: The receipt reports no pending cleanup residue. Successfully installed files remain in place.
packageImportCleanupIncomplete: The receipt reports pending cleanup work.
packageImportRecoveryHint: Inspect VM registration and residue in Tasks and Resources, and complete any necessary recovery before another import. Avoid importing twice or deleting files already in use.
packageImportRecoveryConfirm: I inspected existing VMs and residue, completed necessary recovery and confirm that a new import flow can begin.
packageImportFailureHint: Failure or cancellation does not guarantee rollback. Inspect the receipt for residue and registration state. Parameters were retained; read a new preview and confirm before importing again.
packageExportHostHint: Files are first exported on the device running DroidVM. After export succeeds, use browser package transfers to download them to your current computer or phone.
packageExportLeaveHint: Leaving this page does not cancel a submitted task. Return to query the original request.
packageExportUnavailable: VM package export is unavailable with the current service or permissions.
packageExportPending: An export request is awaiting confirmation. Query its result first. Parameters and the original request are retained without resubmission.
packageExportPathHint: Enter an absolute file path on the device, including the filename. This is not the browser download folder. The parent directory must already exist and be writable.
packageExportVolumeHint: 0 creates one file. Split volumes require at least 16777216 bytes (16 MiB), up to 9223372036854775807. Enter a complete decimal integer without fractions or scientific notation.
packageExportDisksHint: Select disks by slot. Deselect all to export only configuration and boot files without disks.
packageExportStaleDisks: Selected indexes {indexes} are absent from the latest plan. Select the disks again.
packageExportInvalid: Enter a valid absolute file path, compression, exact volume size and disks from the current plan.
packageExportOverwriteWarning: Export may overwrite the destination and matching .NNN volumes. Failure or cancellation may leave partial files. Confirm the destination and disk selection. Configuration changes reject the export and require a fresh plan and confirmation.
packageExportOverwriteConfirm: I confirm these parameters and allow overwriting the destination and matching volumes.
packageExportUnknown: The export result is unknown. Only the original request is queried; it is never resubmitted automatically. A missing record does not prove the export was never executed.
packageExportVolumesResult: Export completed: a main file and {count} .NNN volumes.
packageExportResultHint: The package was written to the host destination. If browser transfers are supported, prepare a download below; include every numbered volume.
packageExportRetryHint: Parameters were retained. Check for partial files, read the plan again and confirm overwriting before retrying. No retry is automatic.
agentRescueKeep: Keep the same temporary VM after the operation and open a rescue terminal
agentRescueKeepWarning: This keeps an interactive maintenance environment; operation results remain separate. Closing or expiry stops the temporary VM and cannot guarantee that the guest has unmounted its file systems.
agentRescueLifetime: Rescue sessions have an absolute 15-minute lifetime. Terminal activity does not extend it. The temporary VM is stopped and cleaned up after expiry.
agentRescueLeaveHint: Leaving this page or disconnecting the terminal only disconnects the browser; it does not close the rescue VM. Refresh the list in this signed-in session to return, or explicitly close it.
agentRescueHandoffHint: A successful rescue handoff does not mean the disk operation or durability succeeded. Review the guest outcome, unmount status and subsequent close result separately.
agentRescueUnavailable: Rescue sessions are unavailable with the current service or permissions.
agentRescueEmpty: No rescue sessions can be recovered for this signed-in session.
agentRescueRemaining: Last observation: {seconds} seconds remaining. Refresh for current status; this is not a live countdown.
agentRescueExpired: Expired; further connections are unavailable. Refresh for cleanup progress.
agentRescueClosing: Stopping and cleaning up the temporary VM.
agentRescueCloseUnknown: The close result is unknown. Only the original request is queried; it will not be resubmitted. Wait for confirmation before another action.
agentRescueCloseDurability: These results describe host stopping, removal and disk synchronization only. They do not prove that the guest unmounted its file systems or fully persisted its writes.
agentRescueCloseWarning: Closing stops the temporary VM and synchronizes the disk. Complete any guest writes and unmounts first; background closing cannot guarantee a clean guest unmount.
agentRescueCloseConfirm: I confirm stopping this rescue VM and understand that a clean guest unmount is not guaranteed.
agentRescueTerminalHint: This terminal connects to the same temporary VM used for maintenance. Input may modify the disk directly; uncertain input is never replayed after disconnection. If the screen is blank, press Enter to display the prompt.
agentRescueMissing: This rescue session cannot currently be connected. Refresh the list to check whether it expired, is closing, or belongs to a different signed-in session.
diskGrowAfterResize: Expand partitions and file systems after resizing
diskGrowEligibility: Available only for a capacity increase with shrinking disabled and a writable disk. For unchanged capacity, use the separate Expand partitions and file systems action.
diskGrowReview: Confirm both steps: enlarge the image, then expand partitions and file systems only after confirmed success and a fresh disk and VM configuration check. Uncertain results, changed configuration or leaving this page stop automatic continuation. Submitted steps can still be queried.
diskGrowSequence: Image capacity → partitions and file systems
diskGrowWaiting: Step 2: waiting for image resizing to succeed.
diskGrowChecking: Step 2: checking capacity and configuration again; not yet submitted.
diskGrowSubmitted: Step 2 was submitted. See the system maintenance task below for results, cleanup and durability. Refreshing only queries the original request.
diskGrowStopped: Step 2 was not submitted automatically. Confirm the image resize result, then review the separate Expand partitions and file systems action. Resizing will not be replayed.
agentPasswordHint: Change the root password in the disk's Linux system. The disk must be offline, writable, and free of shared or backing-disk restrictions.
agentPasswordRule: Use 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, or these symbols: {symbols}
agentPasswordInvalid: The password contains unsupported characters or exceeds the length limit.
agentNormalUsers: Also change passwords for regular users (UID 1000–1999)
agentTargetHint: The operation uses the current disk and VM configuration. Changes before admission reject this request.
agentDiskUnavailable: This disk is unavailable for maintenance: it must be writable, unused, have a complete chain, and have no child disks.
agentGrowHint: Use existing trailing space to grow the last data partition and a supported filesystem. Image capacity stays the same; shrinking is unavailable. Unsupported filesystems or no free space are skipped.
agentAutomaticCleanupHint: The temporary maintenance VM is cleaned up after the operation by default. It is kept only when you explicitly select the rescue option.
agentConfirmWrites: I confirm changes to this disk. Interrupting or cancelling does not roll back changes.
agentUnknown: The request outcome is unknown. Only its original status will be queried; it will not be submitted again. New operations are blocked.
agentSkippedHint: This action was skipped. The partition or filesystem has not been confirmed as expanded.
agentPartialHint: Some actions did not complete. Review each result before deciding what to do next.
agentUncertainHint: Disk changes could not be confirmed. New maintenance operations are blocked in this session; inspect the disk contents first.
agentNoRollback: The disk may already have changed. Cancellation, failure, and cleanup do not restore its earlier contents.
agentRecoveryNeeded: Temporary maintenance resources still need cleanup.
agentRecoveryHint: Clean up abandoned temporary maintenance VMs. Active tasks and ordinary VMs are unaffected.
agentRecoveryConfirm: Stop and remove abandoned maintenance VMs. This does not roll back disk changes or confirm that earlier writes were durable.
agentRecoveryUnknown: The cleanup request outcome is unknown. Only the original request will be queried; cleanup will not be resubmitted.
diskRecoveryHint: Records may include active tasks. Recovery skips active records and attempts remaining file cleanup or registry updates.
diskRecoveryConfirm: Attempt recovery of all eligible disk journal records currently on the host. This may change image files, disk registrations and VM attachments. Once recovery starts it cannot be cancelled. Original operations are not resubmitted. Check disks and attachments after the result arrives.
diskRecoveryResult: Records remaining when this recovery check ended: {count}. Check again later if records remain. An empty journal does not mean the original operation succeeded or its data was rolled back.
diskRecoveryNeeded: The original commit outcome is uncertain. Use disk recovery and inspect disks and attachments before attempting the original operation again.
diskCreateEffect: Create a disk on the host. An overlay depends on its parent and updates references according to the attachment policy.
diskCloneEffect: Copy the selected disk to a new file, preserving its format.
diskResizeEffect: Change the image capacity. Before shrinking, shrink the guest filesystem and partitions.
diskConvertEffect: Convert the image format and optionally relocate its file. The host service coordinates reference updates.
diskFlattenEffect: Copy backing-chain data into this disk to make it independent of its parent.
diskMergeEffect: Merge overlay changes into its parent and update the chain and VM attachments. Parent data will change.
diskResetEffect: Discard all overlay changes and restore the parent's contents.
diskDeleteEffect: Unregister this disk and all descendants, and remove their VM attachments.
diskAttachFollow: Move parent attachments to the new overlay
diskHostPathHint: Enter an absolute folder path on the device running DroidVM.
diskShrinkWarning: Shrinking can permanently truncate data. Verify that partitions and filesystems fit and that you have a backup.
diskDeleteFilesEffect: Image files in the affected set will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
diskKeepFilesEffect: Remove registrations and attachment references while keeping image files.
diskCpuHint: Leave blank for default scheduling, or enter CPU IDs such as 0-3,7.
diskFormInvalid: Check the parameters. The current disk state or backing chain may also prevent this operation.
diskConfirmationHint: The host checks disk and VM reference versions before execution. If another client made changes, reload and review again.
diskAcknowledge: I have reviewed the parameters and impact
diskRecoveryRequired: The commit outcome is uncertain. Check disk recovery in the App before attempting another operation.
diskTaskLink: View or cancel on the tasks page
diskInspectionBusy: Disk in use or file changed; image information cannot be read now
diskInspectionInvalid: Invalid registered path or parent chain
diskReadOnlyHint: A parent disk or a disk referenced directly by multiple slots requires read-only access. This describes saved configuration, not file permissions or current runtime state.
diskChainIncomplete: The parent chain is incomplete or cyclic. Repair the registry relationships first.
diskNoAttachments: No saved VM configuration references found.
diskInspectionHint: Relationships come from the registry and may differ from image headers. Information is read when opened or manually refreshed. A successful read does not mean the disk is idle or writable; native services recheck subsequent operations.
hostDevicesHint: These observations show device nodes and driver files. Their presence does not guarantee virtualization or rendering. Unconfirmed options remain selectable and saved settings are preserved.
hostObservationUnavailable: Host observations are unavailable. Refresh later.
hostHypervisorMissing: The selected hypervisor device node was not detected. Saved settings are preserved; check host support.
hostKgslMissing: No KGSL device was detected. DRM2KGSL rendering availability is unconfirmed.
hostTurnipMissing: The Turnip driver file was not detected. The selected driver’s availability is unconfirmed.
hostSystemBlitFallback: System Vulkan lacks required display-copy extensions and will fall back to CPU copying. Your selection is preserved.
hostBlitPending: Checking system driver extensions. You can continue editing.
hostBlitUnknown: Extension support could not be determined. Unknown does not mean unsupported.
hostBlitMissing: The required extensions below were not detected. This applies to display copying, not to all Vulkan rendering.
hostBlitExtensionsPresent: Required extensions were detected. Actual display copying still needs validation at launch.
hostBlitCacheHint: Extension results are cached until the service restarts. Refresh updates device and driver file observations without loading the system driver again.
cpuTopologyHint: Uses the lowest known capacity among each vCPU’s bound host cores. Unbound vCPUs and those with unknown capacity join the weakest group. The host is read again at launch; manual mode uses the fields below.
cpuTopologyCrosvmOnly: These topology settings are currently used by crosvm only. Other backends preserve them without an effective topology preview.
cpuTopologyWaiting: Host cores are not available yet. Topology cannot be derived.
cpuTopologyInvalid: The binding syntax, vCPU indices or core range cannot be previewed. Review the text configuration.
cpuTopologyUnset: No capacity can be derived: no cores are bound, or their capacities are unknown.
cpuTopologyIncomplete: Some bound cores are missing or have unknown capacity. Only known capacities contribute to this reference; saved bindings are preserved.
cpuTopologySingleCluster: One capacity group uses the default single cluster; no extra cluster is set.
cpuOneToOneHint: Each selected host core maps to one vCPU, in ascending core order. The next step confirms the count and topology changes.
cpuOneToOneChanges: The vCPU count will change from {before} to {after}, bound in order to host cores {hosts}. This replaces all bindings, enables automatic topology, and clears manual capacity and cluster fields. Other settings are preserved.
cpuPickerHint: Grouped by host maximum frequency. Offline or missing saved cores are preserved. Clear binding and Big cores only replace the selection. With one frequency group or all frequencies unknown, Big cores only selects all cores.
cpuFixText: Fix the core binding text or vCPU count before using the picker.
usbRulesPreviewHint: Preview the host's current rules against USB devices without assigning them. VMs that are not running, lack a controller or failed attachment in the current cycle are skipped. Results do not guarantee a later attachment will succeed.
usbRulesPreviewDirty: There are unsaved changes. Save and reread before previewing so results correspond to the displayed rules.
usbRulesPreviewSnapshot: Read at {time}. This is an observation; preview again after device or VM state changes.
usbRulesPreviewConflict: Host rules have changed. Export any draft you need, then reload the rules before previewing.
usbRulesPreviewDefault: No applicable rule; return to host by default
usbRulesPreviewDisabled: Rules are disabled; no automatic assignment
usbRulesPreviewEligible: Currently eligible for automatic assignment. This preview performed no operation.
usbRulesPreviewSkipped: Automatic assignment skips this device; the match is informational.
usbRulesIntro: Rules try exact, port, device and any layers in order, trying available targets in list order within each layer. They apply to the DroidVM host.
usbRulesExactHint: Match both device identity and physical port. Picking a connected device fills both fields.
usbRulesPortHint: Match a physical port path regardless of device identity.
usbRulesDeviceHint: Match device identity regardless of the connected port.
usbRulesAnyHint: Handle devices left unassigned by the first three layers. New rules offer a VM or hiding, as in the App.
usbRulesIdHint: Format: VID:PID or VID:PID:serial. The serial is case-sensitive and identity must exactly match what the device reports.
usbRulesReferenceHint: The current catalog cannot confirm this target is available. Its reference is retained. Check the VM and controller; the host validates saving and attachment.
usbRulesBadId: Use four hex digits for VID and PID, optionally followed by a nonempty serial without line breaks.
usbRulesBadPort: Use a numeric port path separated by dots, such as 1.2.
usbRulesBadController: Choose the default controller or a valid controller ID.
usbRulesBadTarget: Host and hide targets must not include VM or controller references.
usbRulesTargetsKept: The draft and previous catalog are retained. Refreshing targets does not change selected VMs or controllers.
usbRulesBlockedHint: The save failed or is unconfirmed. Your draft is retained. Export changes you need, then reload the host rules to review them. Saving is never retried automatically.
usbRulesUnpersisted: Rules are not confirmed on disk
usbRulesPersistenceHint: Active rules may differ from the file on disk. Review them and explicitly save to confirm persistence.
usbRulesPendingHint: Checking the background save. An unknown result only triggers a lookup of the original request, never a resubmission. Keep this browser session open.
usbRulesSaved: Rules saved and reread from the host.
usbRulesEnableHint: When enabled, DroidVM controls where each USB device goes. Android can only use devices returned to the host by the rules. This toggle edits the draft; saving applies it.
usbRulesSaveHint: Saving immediately applies rules to host USB devices and may change devices used by Android or VMs. If the App or another client has changed the rules, this stale save is rejected.
usbRulesLeaveHint: Your draft and pending task stay in this login session so you can return. Reloading, closing the browser or signing out loses local drafts; accepted background saves are not cancelled.
usbCatalogHint: USB devices connected to the phone running DroidVM and their current state. Global auto-connect rules are not available yet.
usbNoTargets: No running VMs are available for USB attachment. A VM needs an available USB controller.
usbTargetConfirm: Switching disconnects the device from its current target. Safely unmount any device in use before confirming.
usbManualLockHint: Manual switching locks auto-connect for this device. Global rule management is not available yet.
usbAwaitObservation: Waiting for the task to finish and device state to refresh.
usbTargetDone: Task completed. Check the latest device state below.
usbOwnerUnknown: The device is claimed, but its owner is not recorded by DroidVM.
configDirectoryCrosvmHint: crosvm uses virtio-fs with DAX disabled. Legacy type/DAX and read-only values are preserved but do not affect this backend. Root access is off by default; the share uses the app's permissions.
configDirectoryQemuHint: QEMU uses 9P. Cache policy and read-only are applied; timeout, writeback, POSIX ACL and root access values are preserved for crosvm. The cache policy follows QEMU's writeout mapping.
configDirectoryPathInvalid: Enter an absolute host directory path without a trailing slash, dot segments, control characters or reserved filename characters.
configDirectoryTagInvalid: Use a unique mount tag up to 256 characters; avoid reserved filename characters, leading dots or {'@'}, and trailing dots or spaces.
configDirectoryTagDuplicate: This mount tag is already used by another shared directory.
configDirectoryQemuComma: QEMU shared directory paths and tags cannot contain commas.
soundPurposeUnknown: This saved value is not supported by this editor. It is kept until you choose another value.
soundPurposeOutputHint: Affects volume category and how playback interacts with other audio.
soundPurposeInputHint: Affects microphone processing, such as echo cancellation and noise suppression. Availability depends on the device.
configBootDiskChanged: The boot disk changed or was removed. Its pinned boot entry was cleared; review boot settings.
configDetachHint: Removing an entry only detaches it from this VM. Host disks, directories and networks are kept.
resourceDiskReadonlyHint: New attachments are read only by default. Adjust this in disk settings; native validation applies to shared and backing disks.
resourceCatalogHint: Registered resource configurations on the host device.
resourceBacking: Referenced by child disks; attach read only
resourceNotSelectable: This disk cannot currently be selected. Check its registry, backing chain and save status.
sessionLoginHint: Enter a one-time pairing code issued by the DroidVM app on this device.
sessionPairingFormat: 64 lowercase letters (a–f) and digits. Pairing codes expire after 5 minutes.
sessionExpiredHint: Your session has expired or was revoked. Sign in again to continue.
sessionPairingRejected: The pairing code is invalid, expired or already used. Get a new code from the app.
sessionLoginUncertainHint: Check your session before trying a new pairing code.
sessionLogoutUncertainHint: The device has not confirmed revocation. Local data is cleared; retry to finish signing out.
sessionLogoutHint: Sign out of this browser. Running virtual machines keep running.
errorRateLimitHint: Please wait before querying again. No automatic retry will be made.
snapshotHostHint: The VM list was retrieved. Device and service details are not available yet.
httpPreview: API integration · Available actions depend on server capabilities
hostInfoHint: Device and service information appears after connection.
importHint: Local images and VM packages · Unavailable
notFoundHint: Check the address or return to the VM list.
networkHint: Virtual networks, uplink interfaces and addresses
diskHint: Images, parent disk chains and disk operations
resourcesHint: Manage networks, disks and peripherals used by VMs.
resourcesUnavailableHint: Real resources cannot be queried or modified yet.
tasksHint: Once connected, view task progress, results and failure reasons here.
vmsHint: Your VMs and work environments in one place.
createUnavailable: This service does not support VM creation
configNewHint: Defaults have been filled in for this device. Review the name, boot method and required disks before saving.
emptyVmsHint: Connected successfully. This host has no VMs.
noMatchesHint: Try another name or change the status filter.
selectVmHint: Select a VM to view session options
missingVmHint: This resource does not exist or has been removed from the list.
sessionUnavailableHint: A live connection is not available yet. Display and terminal input are unavailable.
name: Name
sessionEntryHint: Session services are unavailable. Only session entry points can be viewed.
errorUnavailableHint: Make sure the management service is running on the host, then check the connection again.
errorInvalidHint: The response cannot be read safely. Check the frontend and backend versions.
errorVersionHint: Update the host app and reload this page, then check the connection again.
errorContextHint: The service restarted or the browser session changed. Previous data was cleared. Check the connection again.
errorAuthHint: Your session is unavailable or expired. Browser sign-in is not connected yet. Check access settings in the host app.
errorPermissionHint: Your account cannot view these resources. Contact the host administrator.
errorUnsupportedHint: Check the host version and device capabilities. Retrying cannot enable an unsupported feature.
errorOfflineHint: Check the network and host status. Reconnecting will fetch the latest data.
errorTimeoutHint: The latest data could not be retrieved. Query again later.
errorUncertainHint: The last action may have completed. Check its status before submitting the same action again.
languageHint: Unsupported browser languages fall back to English.
errorConflictHint: The task state has changed. Refresh its status before choosing another action.
tasksLiveHint: Tasks from this host. Status updates automatically while this page is visible.
tasksRetentionHint: Finished tasks are removed after their retention period. An absent record does not mean an operation never ran.
taskCancelConfirm: Request cancellation of {name}? Work already committed cannot be undone, and cleanup may take time.
taskCancelUnknownHint: Check the task status. Cancellation will not be sent again automatically; a missing record does not confirm cancellation.
taskResultHint: Task completion describes this operation only. Check the resource page to confirm the VM or resource state.
vmControlUncertain: The control acknowledgement is uncertain. Stop the VM to restore a confirmed state.
vmOperationUnknown: The operation outcome is unknown. Status queries will continue; the operation will not be sent again automatically.
vmOperationAdmitted: Operation admitted. Check the actual VM state.
vmOperationWaiting: Operation in progress. Waiting for the result.
vmOperationConfirm: Confirm {action} for “{name}”? Stopping terminates the VM and may lose unsaved data.
vmLogsUnavailableHint: This service does not provide VM logs. Check its version and your permissions.
vmLogReset: The log was cleared or older content was overwritten. Reading resumed from the retained history.
vmLogPartial: Showing part of the log. Load the retained history to read up to 1 MiB.
vmLogTextHint: Displayed as plain text; terminal control commands are not executed.
vmLogEmpty: This log stream has no output yet.
configCopyIdentityHint: A new VM ID and MAC addresses have been generated. Automatic startup is off. Static leases, port forwards and the custom UEFI variables path have been cleared.
configCopyResourcesHint: Disk files are not copied. Choose disks for writable slots; read-only disks and shared directories still use the original paths. VNC screens and serial ports using host paths or USB ACM are disabled for now. Review ports, paths and other host resources before enabling them again.
configProtectionChanged: Protection changed to Normal for the selected backend and hypervisor
configHypervisorMismatch: The selected hypervisor is incompatible with this backend. Choose another.
configPseudoOnly: Pseudo-unprotected mode requires crosvm and Gunyah.
configNotesHint: Preserves Markdown source. Clear the field to remove notes.
configTopologyAuto: Derive CPU topology from core affinity automatically
configAffinityHint: Example: 0=4,5:1=6. Separate vCPUs with colons; use commas or ranges for host cores. Leave blank for no binding. Enter core indices for the actual host device.
configCapacityHint: Example: 0=512,1=1024. Values range from 1 to 1024. Applies only with core affinity and automatic topology disabled.
configClustersHint: Example: 0-3;4-7. Separate clusters with semicolons. Use vCPU indices; a vCPU may not belong to different clusters.
configAffinityInvalid: Check affinity syntax (e.g. 0=4,5:1=6). vCPU indices must be below the processor count; host core indices must be nonnegative integers.
configCapacityInvalid: Use vCPU=capacity (e.g. 0=512,1=1024). vCPU indices must be below the processor count and capacities must be 1–1024.
configClustersInvalid: Check cluster syntax, vCPU index ranges and overlapping clusters (e.g. 0-1;2-3).
configExtraOptionsHint: One argument per line; put argument values on separate lines. Spaces do not split arguments. Blank lines are ignored.
configEnvironmentHint: One NAME=value per line. Values may contain equals signs. The last entry wins for repeated names.
configEnvironmentInvalid: Each environment variable must be NAME=value with a nonempty name.
configUnsupportedShape: This field uses another format. Its value is preserved; edit it in the full JSON view.
configNetworkLeaseHint: Static leases require an L3 network and DHCP on the VLAN; forwarding also requires SNAT. Changes apply on the next start. Address allocation is currently manual; check that the offset is free.
configVlanHint: Empty or 4095 means trunk; 0 is untagged only, and 1–4094 selects a VLAN. Linux bridges do not support untagged-only ports.
configLeaseOffsetHint: Enter a positive offset from the network address. Avoid the gateway, dynamic pool, and addresses already in use.
configMacInvalid: Use six hexadecimal pairs for the MAC address, for example 02:00:00:00:00:01.
configMacRequired: MAC security or an IPv4 static lease requires a configured MAC address.
configLinuxVlanZero: Linux bridges do not support untagged-only ports. Use trunk or a tagged VLAN.
configLeaseOffsetInvalid: An enabled static lease requires a valid address offset greater than 0.
configLeaseOffsetConflict: Another adapter in this VM already uses this offset on the same network and VLAN.
configLeaseOffsetOtherVm: Another VM is configured to use this offset on the same network and VLAN. Choose a different offset.
configLeaseOffsetChosen: Offset selected. Save to apply it.
configLeaseAllocationHint: Selection avoids static leases in the loaded configuration, known gateways and the dynamic pool. It does not reserve an address. Reload before saving if another client changes the configuration.
configLeaseAllocationUnavailable: VLAN address details are unavailable. Check the network or enter an offset manually.
configLeaseNoFreeOffset: No offset is available in this subnet. Check the pool and other adapters' leases.
configLeaseL3Required: Static leases require an L3 network. Existing settings are preserved.
configLeaseVlanMissing: This VLAN is not configured on the selected network. Static leases are unavailable; existing settings are preserved.
configLeaseDhcpDisabled: DHCP for this address family is disabled on the VLAN. Static leases are unavailable; existing settings are preserved.
configLeaseUnknown: DHCP details for this VLAN are unavailable. Check that the network supports static leases.
configForwardSnatDisabled: SNAT for this address family is disabled on the VLAN. Forwarding is unavailable; existing rules are preserved.
configLeaseOffsetRange: The offset is outside the usable subnet range. Network addresses and IPv4 broadcast addresses cannot be used.
configLeaseOffsetGateway: This offset conflicts with the VLAN gateway.
configLeaseOffsetPool: This offset falls inside the dynamic DHCP pool. Choose an address outside the pool.
configForwardsHint: Enter a port such as 80 or a range such as 8000-8010. Host and guest ranges must have equal lengths. Disabling a lease preserves its rules.
configForwards6Gvisor: IPv6 forwarding requires IPv6 SNAT on a gVisor network. Existing rules are preserved.
configForwardProtoInvalid: Choose TCP, UDP, or TCP + UDP.
configForwardPortInvalid: Use ports from 1 to 65535, in ascending ranges such as 8000-8010.
configForwardRangeMismatch: Host and guest port ranges must have equal lengths.
configGpuUdmabuf: Allocate graphics memory in the guest (udmabuf)
configGpuDynamicHint: Disabling guest pool growth preallocates the entire pool and clears the growth step and grant count.
configGpuBlitHint: The host may fall back to CPU copy if the driver lacks the required capabilities.
configGpuCgroup: Bind GPU workers to CPU cores
configGpuCoresHint: For example, 4-7 or 4,6. Use actual core numbers from the host.
configGpuRtHint: Realtime scheduling requires core binding and selected cores. Disabling binding restores normal scheduling.
configGpuCgroupPathInvalid: The CPU group path must be an absolute path starting with /.
configGpuCoresInvalid: Enter a core set such as 4-7 or 4,6.
configGpuRtNeedsCores: Realtime scheduling requires GPU core binding and a valid core set.
configGpuPreallocExceeds: Boot preallocation cannot exceed the guest graphics memory pool.
configGpuGrowthRoom: With a growth step enabled, preallocation must be smaller than the pool.
configGpuStepInvalid: Use 0 or a power of two of at least 2 for the growth step.
configGpuCombinationInvalid: This renderer, acceleration mode, or driver combination is unavailable. Choose a supported combination.
configGpuCoreOverlap: GPU workers and vCPUs share host cores. You can save, but they may compete for CPU time.
configGraphicsAdjusted: Related graphics options were updated. Review the renderer, memory growth, and scheduling settings.
configVpuHint: This setting is retained as in the App. The backend does not yet implement virtio-media codec devices.
configExporterHint: Native display opens in the App. VNC settings control the VM display server.
configTransportHint: The device negotiates the available transport and may fall back. Changing output preserves existing settings.
configNativeCrosvmOnly: Native App display requires crosvm. Change the display output or VM backend.
configVncHostHint: Enter an IPv4 or IPv6 address. 127.0.0.1 is local only; empty means all IPv4 addresses.
configVncHostInvalid: Enter an IPv4 or IPv6 literal without a scheme, port, or zone identifier, or leave empty.
configVncAutoPortHint: Leave empty for automatic assignment; manual ports range from 1024 to 65535.
configVncPortInvalid: Use a port from 1024 to 65535, or leave empty for automatic assignment.
configVncPortConflict: Enabled VNC screens cannot share a port.
configAudioRoutingHint: Endpoints use the phone's audio devices. Changing devices preserves existing purpose settings. Each card supports up to four endpoints per direction.
configAudioMicrophoneHint: Capture uses the phone's microphone and requires recording permission in the phone app. Changing devices preserves existing purpose settings.
audioCatalogueHint: Devices are listed by the phone. Refresh after connecting or disconnecting a device.
audioCatalogueUnavailable: Phone audio devices are temporarily unavailable. Existing bindings are preserved; system routing is still selectable.
audioDeviceMissingHint: This device is not currently listed. Its binding is preserved; choose another device or system routing to change it.
configAudioHostDuplicate: Multiple endpoints in the same direction use the same host device. Remove a duplicate or use system routing.
configSerialPathRequired: This serial backend requires a host path.
configSerialConsoleDuplicate: Only one guest console port can be selected. Select it again.
configSerialSlotDuplicate: Another serial port in this VM already uses this USB ACM slot.
configSerialPtyHint: Optional. A path creates a convenience link to the PTY.
configSerialAcmHint: Slots start at 0. USB ACM must be enabled on the host and the slot must exist; availability is checked at VM start.
configXhciCrosvmHint: crosvm uses only the first xHCI controller with eight USB 2.0 and eight USB 3.0 ports. Other settings are preserved. Removing a controller does not delete automatic attach rules.
configXhciRulesHint: Port counts range from 0 to 15. USB automatic attach rules are managed separately; removing a controller does not delete rules or host devices.
configPeripheralUnsupported: This device type has no supported form or backend yet. Its existing configuration is preserved.
configPeripheralEditUnavailable: Cannot edit this device. Check the collection format, device limit or controller identifier.
configSwiotlbInactive: This protection mode does not use SWIOTLB. The stored value is preserved.
configStoppedOnly: Stop the virtual machine before changing its configuration
configInvalid: Check the configuration format and field values
configSaved: Configuration saved. Close or reload to continue.
configUnknown: The save result is not yet confirmed
configBlocked: Review the configuration before editing again
configKeepDraft: Your draft is retained. Query the result, or export the draft before reloading. The save will not be retried automatically.
configHostPaths: These file paths refer to the host device running DroidVM.
configAdvancedHint: Edit the full VM configuration, preserving untouched fields and the resource ID. Native validation still applies to disk and network references.
configDeleteHint: Deletes only this VM configuration, leaving disk images intact. The virtual machine must be stopped.
configReloadHint: Reloading replaces the current draft. Export any changes you want to keep first.
configSaveHint: Saves against the version loaded when the editor opened. Changes made by another client cause a conflict.
configLeaveHint: There are unsaved or unconfirmed changes. Leaving discards the draft; an accepted background save will continue.
networkBridgeInvalid: Start with a letter; use up to 12 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.
networkDuplicate: This name, interface name or VLAN ID is already in use.
networkL2Linux: L2 bridging requires a Linux bridge.
networkMacInvalid: Enter six colon-separated hexadecimal MAC octets.
networkVlanInvalid: VLAN ID must be 0–4094; 0 means untagged.
networkPdLinux: DHCP-PD requires Linux. Change the bridge type or prefix source.
networkDuidInvalid: DUID must contain colon-separated hexadecimal octets.
networkCidrInvalid: Enter a valid CIDR with room for a gateway and guests. An IPv4 gateway cannot be the network or broadcast address.
networkPoolInvalid: Use positive offsets with end ≥ start; the IPv4 pool must fit inside the subnet.
networkSecondaryLinux: gVisor does not support secondary networks. Switch to Linux to edit or remove them first.
networkUnknownKept: This field format is not editable here. Its original value is preserved.
networkInactiveKept: This parameter is inactive; its value is preserved.
networkEditHint: Configure bridges and VLANs as in the App. Stop the network before saving. Saving does not start it.
networkBlockedHint: The save did not complete. Your draft is retained. Export what you need, then reload the current configuration before editing.
networkPendingHint: Verifying this save. An uncertain receipt is queried without resubmitting.
networkSaved: Saved and reloaded the current network configuration.
networkUplinkHint: Use an App logical interface name such as WiFi, or an actual host interface name.
networkVlanHint: VLAN 0 is untagged. Each VLAN has its own addresses and services.
networkSaveHint: Save this network? The server checks that it is stopped and its original configuration has not changed.
networkLeaveHint: Leave this page? The draft and pending request remain in this session; resume from the network list. Closing the browser loses them.
networkUplinkDiscoveryFailed: Discovery failed. You can still enter an uplink identifier manually.
networkUplinkNoSuggestions: No uplink suggestions are available. You can enter one manually.
networkUplinkUnresolvedHint: This logical identifier currently has no resolved interface. It will be resolved again when the network starts.
networkUplinkPseudoRequired: Using this uplink for L2 bridging requires pseudo bridging.
networkUplinkCustomHint: Suggestions reflect the current host observation. You can keep or enter a custom identifier.
networkObservationHint: These are the observations currently available. Some backend read failures cannot be distinguished, so empty lists do not prove that devices or leases are absent.
networkLiveInactive: The network is not running; live data is unavailable.
networkLiveChanged: State changed during this read. Refresh before acting.
networkLiveBusy: Live observations are unavailable. Refresh later.
networkActionUnknown: The result is uncertain. Only this request is queried; start/stop is not resubmitted.
networkVmReferencesHint: These are saved NIC references, not proof that the VMs are currently attached. The native service checks actual use before stopping.
networkNoObservedRows: No records were observed in this read.
networkActionConfirm: Perform this action on “{name}”? The server checks the observed state and configuration version. Network changes may disconnect this browser. Reconnect and verify an uncertain receipt before doing anything else.
networkDeletionWarning: Delete this network and its NIC references
networkDeletionEffect: This stops the network, deletes its configuration and removes the saved VM NICs listed below. Stopping the network may disconnect this WebUI session.
networkDeletionStopVms: Stop every attached VM first. The host rechecks VM states, the network configuration and reference versions before execution; changes cause deletion to be rejected.
networkDeletionSnapshotHint: This is the frozen snapshot for this confirmation. It is rechecked before execution. Other networks and unrelated NICs are unaffected.
networkDeletionNoAttachments: This snapshot has no attached saved VM NICs.
networkDeletionSucceeded: The deletion task succeeded. A fresh read confirms that the network is no longer registered.
networkDeletionAbsent: Current observation: the network is no longer registered. This observation does not replace the original deletion receipt.
networkDeletionPresent: Current observation: the network is still registered.
networkDeletionUncertain: Configuration persistence is uncertain. Explicitly recover the configuration journal, then verify again. Do not repeat the deletion.
configurationRecoveryConfirm: Recover pending global configuration transactions on the host. These may involve VM, network and disk registry configurations. The catalogues and current configuration will be read again after recovery.
configurationRecoveryNotDeletion: Recovery does not resubmit deletion or prove that the original deletion succeeded or rolled back. The original receipt and current configuration observation are kept separately.
terminalUnavailableHint: Requires administrator access, a host with terminal support and a bidirectional serial stream on a running VM. Agent channels are excluded.
terminalInputUncertain: The last input receipt was lost or only partial. Some keys may already have taken effect. Remaining queued input was discarded and will not be replayed on reconnect. Check the guest first.
terminalInputDiscarded: Some input was not sent because it exceeded the limit, the queue was full or the connection closed. It will not be resent automatically.
terminalOutputReset: Serial output rotated or exceeded the retained range. The terminal was reset and continues from the retained output.
terminalNoStreams: No bidirectional serial stream is available. Enable a serial port in the app or VM configuration, then restart the VM.
terminalResizeHint: Local display: {columns} columns × {rows} rows. This changes only the browser layout. Serial ports cannot negotiate guest window size; if needed, run stty cols {columns} rows {rows} in the guest.
terminalConnectionHint: Hiding the page, closing the terminal or changing streams disconnects it without stopping the VM. Connect manually when you return. Shift+Tab leaves the input area.
terminalPasteHint: Each paste is limited to 2048 bytes and the input queue to 4096 bytes. Output cannot automatically open links or overwrite the clipboard.
transferUnavailable: Browser package transfers are not available on this host.
transferLifetimeHint: Uploads can pause and resume. Reloading the same tab lets you query the original upload; select and verify unfinished files again before resuming. Recovery after logout, closing the tab or restarting the service, and download progress recovery, are not yet supported. Temporary server records expire.
transferFilesHint: Select the main package and every numbered volume together. Only file names and contents are sent; the server uses its own private temporary directory.
transferQuota: Server limits: {files} files; {file} B per file; {session} B per session; {total} B across uploads (not remaining space). Temporary record lifetime: {ttl} seconds.
transferQuotaPending: The server checks file count and storage quotas when the upload starts, then returns its actual limits.
transferSelectionHint: Select exactly one .vmpkg main file and all matching consecutive .001, .002… volumes, up to 1000 files. Names must be distinct UTF-8 basenames of at most 255 bytes.
transferUnknown: The result is unknown. Check the original transfer; no data is replayed automatically.
transferRetry: The server has not acknowledged the pending step. Retry only after this status check.
transferImport: Use this uploaded package for import
transferDeleteUploadHint: Delete the uploaded files and abandon this transfer? Files used by an import or preview cannot be deleted; any refusal will be shown.
transferDownloadHint: Prepare a download from a successful export, then download the main package and each volume. Your browser streams each file directly. Keep the transfer until all browser downloads have finished.
transferHandedOff: Handed to the browser. Check its download manager for progress and completion.
transferDeleteDownloadHint: Release this download record? This can interrupt active browser downloads. A busy server record may remain until its readers close.
transferExistingDownload: Open existing download; release it before preparing another
transferForgetHint: Abandon tracking this transfer? This does not delete files or confirm that the server stopped. Temporary server files may remain until expiry. A new transfer may still be rejected by the quota.
backupScope: App-compatible version 1 JSON containing VM, disk and network configurations. Disk contents, USB rules and App preferences are not included.
backupUnavailable: The current host or session does not provide configuration backup and restore.
backupExportHint: Download a fresh host snapshot directly to the browser. The downloaded file retains exact configuration values. Check your browser for completion.
backupMergeHint: Import merges each category by ID: new IDs are added and matching configurations are updated using the host merge rules. Missing categories are retained. An empty array does not clear existing entries.
backupSizeHint: Import accepts UTF-8 JSON up to {bytes} bytes (31 MiB). A large export may exceed this input limit and cannot be imported here; source data is never silently truncated.
backupReloadHint: The selected file and preview stay in this page session only. Reloading requires selecting the file again. Changing the file, preview or session clears confirmation.
backupPreparing: Uploading configuration and reading the server preview…
backupFileHint: Check the file size, UTF-8 encoding and App backup format, then select or preview again. No persistent configuration is changed before confirmation.
backupPreviewHint: These counts come from the server preview. Matching entries use the imported parameters under the host merge rules, including fields not displayed in this WebUI.
backupEmptyRetained: Empty category: existing entries are retained.
backupCategoryAbsent: Not included: existing entries are retained.
backupOrderHint: Networks are committed first, then VMs and disks together. If the later step fails, completed categories remain changed; the operation is not one transaction across all categories.
backupConfirm: I reviewed the category changes and understand that matching IDs will be updated using the host's merge rules.
backupUnknown: The commit receipt is unknown. Query the original request; it will not be submitted again automatically.
backupRecoveryRequired: The host reports that configuration recovery is required. Review the affected configurations and resolve recovery in the host before another import.
backupSucceeded: Configuration import completed. The displayed catalogs have been refreshed.
backupPartialHint: Some categories may already have changed. Review the VM, disk and network catalogs and any host recovery requirement. A new import starts a new workflow; it does not resume or roll back this request.
backupRecoveryConfirm: I checked the current configurations and handled the reported recovery requirement.
backupRestart: Start a new workflow after review
settingsVmHint: Choose a VM to edit its configuration using the same categories as the App.
settingsUsbRulesHint: Manage the host’s existing USB auto-connect rules.
settingsCapabilityUnavailable: Not available from the current host or with this session’s permissions.
settingsAppPreferencesHint: These preferences are currently managed in the host App. Host options such as log clearing and automatic hugepage reservation are still awaiting shared settings support in WebUI.
settingsTransferHint: Upload package files from this browser or download a completed export.
settingsHostServiceHint: Service start, stop and restart controls are not available through this WebUI. Manage the host service in the App.
backupUnknownResult: The task ended without a trustworthy category receipt. Some changes may already be persistent; this is not confirmation that nothing changed.
webServiceIntro: Manage the WebUI HTTP and WebSocket service using the host App’s settings. Service changes do not restart the daemon or stop running VMs.
webServiceUnavailable: The current host or session does not provide WebUI service management.
webServiceMenuHint: Configure HTTP/WS access, listening scope and port, or restart the WebUI service.
webServiceReconnectHint: A lost connection or receipt does not prove that the change failed. Query the original request when access returns. If the address changes or access is disabled, check the WebUI page in the host App.
webServiceStale: This is the last observed status; it has not been confirmed for the current connection.
webServiceDiscoveryFailed: Network discovery failed. The service may have fallen back to local access; the requested access settings are not verified as applied.
webServiceListenFailed: The requested listener could not start. Check the port and host network; local fallback does not confirm that the requested settings were applied.
webServiceWriteFailed: The settings write result requires recovery. Re-read WebUI settings in the host App, then refresh this page. Browser controls cannot perform this recovery.
webServiceApplyPending: A service change is waiting to be applied. The addresses below still describe the current listener.
webServiceAddressHint: Addresses are shown for reference. Changing the port or external origin may require opening the new address and signing in again; this page does not redirect automatically.
webServiceScopeHint: Local-network listening is the default. Access across networks also depends on the host’s routing and network configuration.
webServiceOriginsHint: At most 8 exact HTTP origins, one per line, such as http://example.test:8080. Use ASCII and omit paths, spaces, credentials, queries and fragments.
webServiceInvalid: Check the port and external HTTP origins before continuing.
webServiceReloadDraftHint: Reading settings again replaces unsaved form values with the current host settings.
webServiceRestartSavedHint: Restart uses the last read, saved settings. Unsaved form changes will not be submitted.
webServiceDisconnectHint: Saving or restarting can disconnect HTTP and WebSocket sessions. Running VMs are unaffected. The task receipt only confirms saving or queuing; read status again after the host applies the change.
webServiceDisableHint: Disabling WebUI may disconnect this browser. Re-enable it from the host App; the browser cannot turn an unavailable service back on.
webServiceConfirm: I reviewed these settings and understand that this browser connection may be interrupted.
webServiceTaskHint: Task completion means settings were saved or a restart was queued. It does not prove that the listener has applied the change.
webServiceUnknown: The operation receipt is unknown. Query the original request; do not repeat the save or restart.
webServiceApplied: Verified applied: settings match, no application is pending, and the reported listener state is consistent.
webServiceQueued: The host acknowledged saving or queuing. Application has not yet been verified.
webServiceNotApplied: The latest status does not confirm the requested service state. Review the host error and actual settings before another operation.
webServiceOutcomeHint: The operation ended but its requested state is not verified. Review the latest host status. A new workflow uses those current settings and does not replay the previous request.
webServiceOutcomeConfirm: I checked the current service state and any host recovery requirement.
webServiceRestartWorkflow: Start a new workflow after checking
webServicePairingHint: Pairing codes and local service recovery remain in the host App. No pairing code is generated or displayed here.
imageImportMenuHint: Register an existing host image and its complete backing chain.
imageImportIntro: Register an existing raw or qcow2 image in the host disk catalog. Source files are neither copied nor rewritten. Keep the image and its backing files at their host locations.
imageImportUnavailable: Image import is unavailable for this host or account.
imageImportSourceHint: Enter a file path on the host running DroidVM. For a file on your browser device, first save it to the host using the upload area above. This page does not download from online image sources.
imageImportPlanHint: The complete chain runs from the selected image to its deepest backing file. Confirmation submits against the inspected disk and VM configuration versions. Changed files or configuration require a new inspection.
imageImportNoAttachments: This plan does not change VM disk attachments.
imageImportConfirm: I reviewed the complete backing chain, new registrations and VM attachment changes, and confirm this import plan.
imageImportUnknown: The request result is not confirmed. Only the original request is queried; it is never resent automatically. Keep this page open.
imageImportRegistered: The host reports the image registered. Check the task state and any recovery notice.
imageImportRecoveryHint: Registration may be incomplete or uncertain. Check the disk catalog and complete any required configuration recovery in the host App before starting a new import. Do not delete registered images to retry.
imageImportSuccess: Image registration completed and the disk catalog was refreshed.
imageImportCreateHint: View this disk or open the existing VM creation page. Select the disk in Storage and check the boot settings. Disks are attached read only by default; review this for your intended use.
imageImportRestartHint: Check the disk catalog and this result before another import. Complete any host recovery first. A new workflow inspects files and configuration again.
imageImportOutcomeConfirm: I checked the disk catalog and this result, and completed all required host recovery.
imageImportRestart: Start a new workflow after checking
linuxVmTitle: Create Linux from an existing image
linuxVmMenuHint: Copy a registered image, prepare its Linux disk and review VM configuration.
linuxVmIntro: Copy the image, convert the copy to qcow2 if needed, prepare it step by step, then review VM configuration. Each step requires an explicit action. The new VM does not start automatically.
linuxVmUnavailable: This creation workflow is unavailable for the current host or account.
linuxVmSelectHint: Select an available raw or qcow2 Linux image suitable for this host architecture. Import an existing host file first if it is not registered.
linuxVmCloneHint: Choose a host parent directory and copy filename, then confirm copying into a subdirectory named after the VM. The subdirectory is created if missing. The copy keeps the source format without compression; later steps prepare only the copy and retain the original image.
linuxVmConvertHint: Convert a raw copy to uncompressed qcow2. An existing qcow2 copy needs no conversion. Conversion keeps the copy at its host location.
linuxVmFlattenHint: If the copy still depends on a backing file, flatten it into an independent disk first. Continuing will explain when flattening is not required.
linuxVmResizeHint: You can increase the copy's capacity. Shrinking is unavailable in this wizard. Explicitly skip if no increase is needed; filesystem growth is a separate later step.
linuxVmPasswordHint: Set the copy's root password in the password dialog. The password is entered only for this step and cleared after submission. If skipping, make sure you already have a working login method.
linuxVmGrowHint: Expand partitions and filesystems inside the copy to use available space. Skip if unnecessary. Incomplete tasks retain their actual results.
linuxVmConfigureHint: Review the six App configuration categories. Adjust CPU, memory and networking here. The VM is created only after you confirm saving.
linuxVmDiskConstraints: This wizard uses an uncompressed qcow2 copy and only increases capacity. Filesystem growth is confirmed separately in a later step.
linuxVmKeepCopy: A successfully created copy is retained. Failed preparation, skipping or leaving the wizard does not delete it. Check the disk catalog.
linuxVmSkipHint: This step will be marked skipped and remain visible in the final results. Disk changes that already happened are not undone.
linuxVmBlockedHint: The task result is unconfirmed or requires recovery. Query the original task and complete any host recovery. Completing recovery does not mean this step succeeded.
linuxVmResultHint: Completed, skipped and failed preparation steps are listed separately. Uncertain results only query the original task; they cannot continue or retry automatically.
linuxVmCreatedHint: The VM configuration was saved without starting it. Check the step results for any unfinished preparation.
linuxVmLeaveHint: This browser session retains wizard progress. Submitted tasks keep running; unsubmitted confirmations close and passwords are cleared. No next step starts automatically and the copy is not deleted.
imageUploadIntro: Upload one standalone raw or qcow2 image from your browser device, save it on the host, then inspect and register it. Browser uploads of images with backing chains are not supported yet.
imageUploadUnavailable: Image file uploads are unavailable for this host or account.
imageUploadLifetime: Uploads enter a temporary cache; finishing does not save them to a persistent directory. Leaving pauses transmission. Within the same tab, login session and service run, reload to query the original record, then reselect and verify unfinished files before continuing. Host quotas and expiry apply.
imageUploadFileHint: Select one nonempty image file. The host checks its actual format and whether it is standalone.
imageUploadInstallHint: The upload cache is ready. After you confirm the destination, the host checks the image and saves it to persistent storage. The destination directory must already exist. Existing files cannot be overwritten.
imageUploadConfirm: I checked the host directory and filename and confirm saving the image there.
imageUploadUnknown: The save result is unconfirmed. Only the original request is queried; saving is not repeated automatically. You cannot delete the upload cache or start a new workflow until the result is known.
imageUploadRecoveryHint: The save result or durability is uncertain. Retain this result, inspect the host directory and complete any recovery requested by the host. Do not register the image yet or delete the destination file to retry.
imageUploadInstalled: The image was saved with confirmed durability. You can now pass this path to the image inspection and registration workflow below.
imageUploadIncomplete: This task did not confirm a complete save. Check the error and host files before deciding what to do next.
imageUploadImport: Use this path to inspect and import
imageUploadImportBusy: An existing image import needs attention
imageUploadImportBusyHint: The existing import path, plan and task were preserved. Complete its status lookup or outcome review below, then try this button again.
imageUploadHandedOff: The persistent file path is now in the form below. Select “Inspect image and backing chain”, review its plan, then confirm registration.
imageUploadRemoveHint: Delete only this upload's temporary cache. An image successfully saved to the host directory is retained. This action is unavailable while the save result is uncertain.
imageUploadResetHint: A new workflow clears tracking on this page. The host expires any remaining cache; saved images are retained. Check this result first.
imageUploadOutcomeConfirm: I checked this upload and save result and confirm starting a new workflow.
graphicUnavailable: This display is unavailable. For browser graphics, configure a VNC display and start the VM.
graphicFullscreenFallback: Browser full screen is unavailable. The console continues using the available page area.
graphicInput: Type here to send text to the VM
graphicInputHint: Tap or drag on the display to control the pointer; use two fingers to scroll. Focus the display for physical keyboard input. Leaving this window disconnects the session; reconnect explicitly.
graphicReason_not_vnc: Native display is not available in the browser
graphicReason_not_running: Start the virtual machine to connect
hostOverviewHint: Live observations from the device running DroidVM. Unknown values remain unavailable.
hostOverviewMenuHint: Device, service, resources and registered virtual machines.
hostCpuUnknown: Waiting for a valid CPU sampling window
hostMemoryHint: Available memory is the kernel MemAvailable estimate, including reclaimable memory.
hostStorageHint: The filesystem containing DroidVM data. Available space may exclude reserved blocks; usage is total minus free space.
hostUnsupported: This host does not provide overview access.
hostStaleHint: Showing an older observation. Refresh to obtain current values.
hostInventoryHint: Counts are observations from separate services and may differ briefly during changes. They are not one atomic snapshot.
hostDiskVirtualUnknown: No cached virtual capacity is available. This view does not scan image files.
hugepagesMenuHint: Reserve pool, CMA and acquisition progress
hugepagesIntro: Manage the host reserve of 2 MiB pages. Saved targets and current values are shown separately.
hugepagesAcquireHint: Mode 1 scans; mode 2 migrates and reclaims; mode 3 evicts per block. Acquisition may reclaim system caches.
hugepagesTargetsHint: Enter counts of 2 MiB pages. Targets are saved and applied when supported. The kernel may adjust them; check live values afterwards.
hugepagesCmaHint: Leave empty to keep the CMA target; enter 0 to turn it off.
hugepagesInvalidTarget: Enter integers from 0 to 1073741824. The pool target must meet the VM minimum.
hugepagesBusy: Another operation is using hugepage configuration. Refresh shortly.
hugepagesStale: Showing the last successful observation. Refresh failed; changes are paused.
hugepagesTaskHint: A completed task means the control operation ended, not that the pool is full. Check current kernel acquisition state.
hugepagesUnknown: The receipt is unknown. Only the original request is queried; it is not resubmitted.
hugepagesPartial: The operation may be partially applied or lack a complete receipt. Review live and saved values before further changes.
hugepagesConfirmStop: Request that the current acquisition stop? Pages already acquired are retained.
hugepagesConfirmTargets: Save pool target {pool} and CMA total target {cma}?
hugepagesManagementUnavailableHint: This daemon or session supports only the basic hugepage controls shown below. Existing pending operations can still be queried.
hugepagesModuleHint: Runtime controls affect the current pool. Enabling restores the saved target and requests one gentle acquisition.
hugepagesConsumersBlockStop: Stop the consuming virtual machines before disabling or unloading the module.
hugepagesBootHint: This setting takes effect at the next device boot. It does not load or unload the running module.
hugepagesCmaIntro: Try the reservoir live, check its behavior, then explicitly save it for the next module load.
hugepagesCmaUnavailable: CMA controls are unavailable while the module is unloaded or unsupported.
hugepagesCmaRisk: Changing movable-memory routing may destabilize the kernel or restart the device. The trial is live only and is not saved for the next boot.
hugepagesCmaSaveHint: Saving records the current live target and selected method. It does not start another acquisition. The live method must still match, unless the kernel already allows CMA.
hugepagesCmaBelowSavedPool: The live CMA total is below the saved pool target. Update the reserve targets before saving this CMA configuration.
hugepagesAdvancedIntro: Saved values and module readback are separate. Boot settings always describe the next module load, even when the numbers match.
hugepagesAdvancedSystemReserveHint: Sets the reserve established when the module loads. Changing it requires explicit confirmation.
hugepagesAdvancedCmaFloorHint: Minimum CMA reservoir size; it can apply live when the module exposes a writable control.
hugepagesAdvancedBootAcquireHint: 0 disables acquisition; 1 scans, 2 migrates and reclaims, and 3 evicts per block.
hugepagesAdvancedBootRunsHint: Number of acquisition passes requested when the module next loads.
hugepagesAdvancedBootWaitHint: Waiting interval for the module load-time acquisition sequence.
hugepagesAppliesLive: A non-empty value can be applied live. Restoring the default waits for the next load.
hugepagesAppliesNextLoad: Applies at the next module load. A matching readback does not prove it is in effect now.
hugepagesReloadRequired: Saved and current values differ; a module reload is required for the saved setting.
hugepagesAdvancedRange: Integer from {minimum} to {maximum}. Leave empty to restore the module default.
hugepagesAdvancedInvalid: Enter an integer within the displayed range, or leave empty.
hugepagesMaintenanceHint: These actions change module state only when explicitly confirmed. Refreshing this page only reads state.
hugepagesReconcileHint: Ask the module to reconcile its hugepage ownership counters. This may change reported usage.
hugepagesMigrateHint: Remove the obsolete CMA probe setting so it no longer disables CMA on the next module load.
hugepagesDismissCrashHint: Clear the module crash marker after reviewing the device state. This does not diagnose or fix the cause of the crash.
hugepagesConfirmRuntimeEnable: Enable or restore the pool from saved settings, then request one gentle acquisition?
hugepagesConfirmRuntimeDisable: Stop acquisition and disable the current reserve? Saved boot settings remain available for a later enable.
hugepagesConfirmUnload: Stop acquisition and unload the hugepage module from the running kernel?
hugepagesConfirmBootEnable: Enable the hugepage module at the next device boot?
hugepagesConfirmBootDisable: Disable the hugepage module at the next device boot?
hugepagesConfirmCmaTrial: Try a live CMA total of {target}, using {lever}? Nothing is saved for the next load.
hugepagesConfirmCmaDisable: Disable live CMA routing and the reservoir, and save the disabled state?
hugepagesConfirmCmaSave: Save the observed CMA total {target} and method {lever} for the next load?
hugepagesUnloadRisk: Unloading removes the pool and its live ownership tracking. All consuming virtual machines must be stopped first.
hugepagesSystemReserveRisk: This changes the memory reserve created at module load. An unsuitable value can leave too little memory for the host or virtual machines.
hugepagesRiskAcknowledgment: I understand this change and want to continue.
hugepagesCmaSavedMethodHint: Saving this method does not guarantee it will be restored automatically after a device restart. Check the actual state after restarting.
hpProcessIntro: Inspect hugepage attribution or THP usage of running virtual machines. Process controls apply only to a verified process identity.
hpProcessKoCoverage: Lists the owners recorded by the hugepage module. Unverified legacy ownership is identified separately.
hpProcessScanCoverage: Reads THP usage only for running virtual machines. This is not a scan of all host processes and does not establish reserve-pool ownership.
hpProcessFallback: Module ownership is unavailable; the automatic view is using running VM THP measurements.
hpProcessUnavailable: This source is currently unavailable. Missing measurements are not zero usage.
hpProcessPartial: The observation is incomplete. Exited, changed or unreadable processes may have unknown usage.
hpProcessKnownTotal: Readable records only: {value}. This is not the complete total.
hpProcessScanAttribution: THP measured for this running VM
hpProcessControlsCurrentVm: Controls target the verified current VM process, not the unverified owner of the legacy KO record.
hpProcessRowIncomplete: Some details could not be read or verified. Unknown values remain unavailable.
hpProcessDStateHint: D means uninterruptible kernel sleep. A signal may not take effect until that wait completes.
hpProcessStale: Showing the previous observation. Refresh failed; process actions are paused.
hpProcessEmpty: No process entries were reported by this source.
hpProcessEmptyPartial: No readable entries were returned. The incomplete observation does not prove there is no usage.
hpProcessPoolPending: A hugepage control operation is unresolved. Query its original receipt before sending process signals.
hpProcessUnknown: The signal result is unknown. Further signals are blocked; only the original request is queried. It is never automatically resubmitted or escalated to KILL.
hpProcessSignalSent: The signal was sent to the verified process.
hpProcessSignalNotSent: Successful signal delivery was not confirmed.
hpProcessConfirmedExited: The original process is confirmed to have exited.
hpProcessReceiptHint: A sent signal does not prove that the process exited or released its memory. Check a fresh observation.
hpProcessConfirmVm: Associated VM: {name}. Terminating this process may stop the VM.
hpProcessTermRisk: TERM asks this exact process to terminate. It may ignore the request; unsaved work may be lost if it exits.
hpProcessKillRisk: KILL forcibly terminates this exact process without normal cleanup. Unsaved VM data may be lost.
hpProcessSignalAcknowledgment: I checked the process identity and accept the effect of this signal.
hpProcessStackUnavailable: The stack could not be read. The process may have exited, changed state or become inaccessible.
hpProcessStackTruncated: The stack reached the display limit and was truncated.
imageImportOptimizeHint: Check this disk and shared defaults before confirming optimization. Registering an image does not rewrite it.
